### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/dogfood`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b76df9a6980d935c194f778e7eb10aca382aac4c`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `master_detail (literal, 45 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b76df9a6980d935c194f778e7eb10aca382aac4c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b4dcfdaa408117b20a48cb393f72f5594006412e` — the merge of head `ae8ecd6235d6ae8e92d8e7f67ea755570381a65d` into base `b76df9a6980d935c194f778e7eb10aca382aac4c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b4dcfdaa408117b20a48cb393f72f5594006412e && git checkout b4dcfdaa408117b20a48cb393f72f5594006412e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b76df9a6980d935c194f778e7eb10aca382aac4c ae8ecd6235d6ae8e92d8e7f67ea755570381a65d && git checkout -B drift-repro b76df9a6980d935c194f778e7eb10aca382aac4c && git merge --no-ff ae8ecd6235d6ae8e92d8e7f67ea755570381a65d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b76df9a6980d935c194f778e7eb10aca382aac4c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b76df9a6980d935c194f778e7eb10aca382aac4c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `ae8ecd6235d6ae8e92d8e7f67ea755570381a65d`

review (review-b, areas S2+S4) · 2026-11-15T10:50Z · I read the full diff at this head against GitHub: 4 files, +544/−24, all under `packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf/**`. I also read report 6893177082 and addendum 6893156419, card #33701, and `SharingService#buildReadFilter` on this tree. The main question was whether each leg exercises the path it claims, since these numbers become filing evidence.

### Does each leg exercise its path?

1. **R9 `--shares`: yes.**
   - Rows are written as the sharing service reads them: `object_name`, `recipient_type: 'user'`, `recipient_id` = member, `access_level: 'read'`. They are also filtered to the table's real columns, and the run fails on an unfilled NOT NULL column.
   - They are spread over non-owned accounts, never the head of the table.
   - Controls in the same harness:
     - the member total equals owned + shared at 900 and 5000 grants;
     - the shares-0 run reads only what the member owns;
     - by-id reads of the first and last granted account;
     - the bind count moves 4 → 902 under `--sql-log`.
   - The H2 reading (6000 of 7000 visible; the 6000th grant answers 404 `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`) matches the `engine.find('sys_record_share', … limit: 5000)` read in `buildReadFilter` on this tree, with 5000 grants as the control.
2. **R10 roll-up pairs: yes.**
   - The three pairs are identical but for 0, 1 and 2 `summary` fields, and the 0-field pair is the control.
   - Parents are seeded with their true totals, so a recompute writes a real value.
   - Every call writes different values (`body(call)`), so no update is a no-op.
   - Statement counts come from `Server-Timing` and are exact on both dialects. The +4 statements per recompute per field matches the captured text.
3. **R8 proxy and grants cache: yes.**
   - Only the measuring boot goes through the proxy; the seed is direct.
   - Each chunk is held rttMs/2 each way, with equal-delay timers so order is preserved.
   - The injected RTT is measured (`select 1` direct vs proxied) rather than assumed, and the chunk counts show the traffic really went through the proxy.
   - The cache posture comes from the server's own `[authz-cache]` boot line, with a warning if that line is missing.
4. **`--sql-log`.** It captures the lines the server log gained during one warm request and prints any scenario whose logged count differs from `Server-Timing`. The README says a `--sql-log` run is for shapes, not milliseconds.
5. **micro I9 and I10.** Both compare the answer as well as the time, and I9 labels the 5000-cap difference as intended.

### Deviations judged

- **Repo-wide `pnpm lint` not run locally: accepted.** `Lint · ESLint` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are `success` on this head.
- **Whole `@objectstack/dogfood` typecheck left to CI: accepted.** `TypeScript Type Check` and `Type Check · workspace` are `success`. The fixture's red-then-green through the dogfood tsconfig is recorded.
- **PostgreSQL with `fsync=off` and `synchronous_commit=off` throughout: accepted.** It is declared in the PR body and the addendum. Statement counts, which carry the R10 ranking, are exact; write milliseconds are understated and should be quoted that way.
- **Numbers stamped on engine tree `a557fa38`, not re-benched after the final main merge: accepted.** The incoming merge touched nothing under `bench/`, and each result file carries its commit.

### Filing caveats for the seat (no change to this PR)

These belong to the M2 cards, per #33751 §1 lesson 5:

- **I9 is a statement pair in isolation, not what a member request emits.** Its "today" and "target" both omit what the engine can add around the share scope. The real `buildReadFilter` also ORs in:
  - the pending-approval read grants (`pendingApproverReadGrants`);
  - the queue-sitting match (`queueSittingMatch`), when the member is in a queue;
  - and the request carries the tenant wall.

  The fixture has no approvals and no queues, so "same answers" holds here only. Quote "PG 21.6 → 7.0 ms" as the scope statements alone. End to end, most of the R9 growth is rows read (the addendum says so). The R9 card must keep the approval and queue arms inside the subquery shape and carry the epic's parity test.
- **R10 inserts accumulate on parents 100–109** across iterations, so the aggregate reads a few more children per call as a run goes on. That does not touch the statement counts, but `createMany` milliseconds drift slightly upward within a run.
- **H2 (class a, fail-closed: an under-grant, not a leak)** is reported, not filed. `Fixes #33701` closes the card on merge, so the M2 cards the addendum ranks and the H2 card should be filed by the seat before or at landing, so the card's "file what pays" half is not lost.

### Other checks

- **Scope.** No product code. `@objectstack/dogfood` is `private: true`, and `skip-changeset` is correct. The declarations are `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, and both are right.
- **Card relation.** `Fixes #33701` is correct: the card's output is legs + numbers + addendum, and filing is the seat's. No closing keyword sits next to another open card.
- **Ablation.** Not applicable: there are no test pins, and each leg carries its own control.
- **Check-runs at this head.** 29 `success` (including `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core` and Test Core 4–5/8), 21 skipped, and 3 still running (Test Core 1–3/8), with no failures. Landing waits for those to be green.
- **Author.** `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay write).
